title: Why is taxi number 1729 so special?
description:
In 1913, Srinivasa Ramanujan, a clerk at the Madras Port Trust, sent a letter full of formulas to G. H. Hardy in Cambridge. Years later, Hardy visited the ill Ramanujan and called his taxi number, 1729, rather dull – but Ramanujan instantly saw that it is the smallest number that is a sum of two cubes in two different ways.

One true story from the history of math – every day.
Created with AI assistance (animation and voice); facts from the sources listed.

Sources:
